sectors.trend: Iron ore weakness pressures majors; however, rare earths (Lindian, Barkly 99% magnet extraction) and gold exploration (Great Southern, Kaiser) show active pipeline. Uranium (Infini) and phosphate (Aguia) also advancing.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face near-term headwinds from soft iron ore; small-cap rare earths and gold explorers offer speculative upside. Diversification within materials is key.

sectors.trend: Oil at $86 on Hormuz tensions benefits upstream (Woods Point, Oil Search) but raises input costs for downstream and transport. Danish wind farm entry signals renewable pipeline. One Nation's coal/nuclear stance adds policy uncertainty in Victoria.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, OSG.AX see positive oil-driven sentiment; WES.AX, AGL.AX face mixed signals. Policy risk around nuclear/coal in Victoria creates volatility for energy names.

sectors.trend: Rocketing rate expectations pressure bank valuations via discount rates but support NIM. Property credit crash post-budget tax changes threatens mortgage book quality. Macquarie/KPMG $700m audit bid signals M&A activity.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face valuation compression from higher rates but benefit from rate income. Property-linked credit risk is a watch item. MQG.AX audit bid is a positive catalyst.

sectors.trend: Woolworths (WES.AX) to stop Tassie beef sales; August data shows 'dupe' brand shift and weight-loss drug demand. Qantas (QAN.AX) strike vote adds travel sector risk. Renter relief is a positive for housing-adjacent names.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, CWP.AX face supply-chain and consumer-preference shifts. QAN.AX strike risk is a near-term negative. Renter relief supports REIT and construction names modestly.

sectors.trend: August home values declined sharply; auction sentiment deteriorated; property investor credit growth crashed. Bathla developer near collapse. Insurer short-changing on claims adds stress.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) and property developers face headwinds. Credit contraction limits new supply. Insurance sector (WBC.AX, CGU.AX) under regulatory scrutiny.

sectors.trend: Australia flagged as missing AI economic boom due to slow uptake. Meta $24b settlement and social media ban loom. SpaceX/AI data centre disruption discussed.
sectors.implications: Structural concern for ASX tech (WBC.AX, XRO.AX, SPL.AX). AI under-adoption is a long-term productivity drag. Meta settlement may affect advertising revenue flows.

key_themes: Geopolitical oil shock: Hormuz strikes driving $86 WTI, inflation risk, and RBA hawkish repricing
Australian property correction: falling values, credit contraction, developer distress
RBA rate path: market pricing higher-for-longer amid oil-driven inflation
Resource sector bifurcation: iron ore weakness vs. rare earths/gold/uranium exploration momentum
Corporate distress: Star Entertainment, Bathla, and insurer conduct issues
Structural AI gap: Australia's slow AI uptake as a long-term growth risk
Energy transition policy uncertainty: coal/nuclear debate in Victoria vs. renewable investment

risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure; maintain cash buffers; monitor WTI above $90 as escalation trigger
Reduce duration in fixed income; favour floating-rate and short-duration credit; underweight rate-sensitive REITs
Avoid distressed developers (Bathla); favour investment-grade bank paper; monitor NAB/CBA property loan write-downs
Diversify away from pure iron ore exposure; favour copper, gold, and rare earths within materials
Reduce QAN.AX position ahead of strike vote outcome; monitor travel sector sentiment
Avoid speculative small-caps with auditor qualification flags; monitor SGH.AX and Bathla closely

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 likely under pressure from oil-driven inflation fears, RBA hawkish repricing, and property sector weakness. Geopolitical volatility from Hormuz strikes creates two-way risk. Expect 2-4% index volatility. Banks and upstream energy outperform; property, iron ore, and consumer discretionary lag.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural concerns around AI under-adoption and property credit contraction cap upside. However, rare earths, gold, and renewable energy pipelines offer medium-term growth. RBA likely holds or hikes once more before easing cycle resumes in H2 2026. Iron ore recovery contingent on China stimulus.
